CSE - Open Callback VI Reference.vi

Owning Palette: CSE Script Processor

The VI opens a VI reference to a CSE Callback VI, prepares it for execution, and saves its path for a further use. A Callback VI reference can then be passed to CSE - Execute Parsed Script.vi that will call the Callback VI to be under control of it.

Details

Click the parameters for more information

 

CSE RefNum is a reference number for a CSE instance that contains a parsed CSE script. CSE - Parse Script.vi returns a value that can be wired directly to this terminal.
Callback VI Path specifies an absolute path of CSE Callback VI to which a reference need be opened.
Window Title. If you pass a non-empty string to it, the VI assigns the string to a window title of the Callback VI. It can be helpful when a Callback VI should work interactively.
error in describes error conditions that occur before this VI runs. This input provides standard error in functionality.
status indicates error status.
code contains error code.
source contains additional error information.
Save w/o diagram (F). If TRUE, the VI saves a Callback VI without the block diagram to a file in a system temporary directory and then deletes the file. This option can be reasonable when a Callback VI is a VI template. By default, Save w/o diagram is FALSE.
dup CSE RefNum is a flow-through parameter with the same value as CSE RefNum.
Callback VI RefNum returns a strictly typed VI refnum that contains a reference to the CSE Callback VI opened.
error out contains error information. This output provides standard error out functionality.
status indicates error status.
code contains error code.
source contains additional error information.

 

CSE - Open Callback VI Reference.vi - details

CSE calls a Callback VI through Call By Reference Node that requires a strictly typed VI refnum. On this reason, a Callback VI must have the same connector pane as CSE Callback Template.vit supplied. A Callback VI can be either a regular VI or a VI template. If it is a VI template, a new unique instance of it will be created unless the template itself is already in memory. Use "Tools >> CalcExpress >> Open CalcExpress Template..." menu to open the CSE Callback Template.vit.

If you use this VI to open a reference to a Callback VI, a script called from another script has opportunity to inherit a path of the Callback VI from its caller. This way, all CSE instances involved in a call chain of the top-level script will use the same Callback VI (but different VI instances if it's either a VI template or a reentrant VI).
